commit c0e7676c5b634b733cd8d40bb8d954c6b5fa6cf7
Author: Петушков А. <96879250+marko1olo@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 29 15:03:44 2026 +0400

    fix(retry): skip the content-length checkpoint for HEAD and for a 206 without content-range (#5610)
    
    * fix(retry): do not checkpoint HEAD responses from content-length
    
    onResponseStart derives the resume checkpoint from content-length without
    looking at the method, so a HEAD gets this.end = content-length - 1 while
    its body is legitimately empty. onResponseEnd then requires
    this.start === this.end + 1 and throws RequestRetryError('Content-Range
    mismatch'); 200 is not a retryable status, so the request fails outright.
    A HEAD has no body to checkpoint, so leave this.end null.
    
    Signed-off-by: marko1olo <marko1olo@users.noreply.github.com>
    
    * fix(retry): forward 206 without content-range instead of asserting
    
    parseRangeHeader returns { start: 0, end: null, size: null } for an absent
    or empty value and only returns null when a value is present and fails the
    regex, so the `range == null` guard in the first-206 branch never fires for
    a response that has no content-range at all. Execution falls through to
    `assert(end != null && Number.isFinite(end), 'invalid content-length')`,
    which throws AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION] out of onResponseStart before
    any data reaches the handler.
    
    RFC 9110 15.3.7.2 requires a server to omit the top-level content-range on
    a multipart/byteranges response, since each part carries its own, so a
    compliant server answering a multi-range request trips this.
    
    A content-range that matches the regex always yields a numeric end, so
    widening the guard to range.end == null only adds the absent and empty
    cases. Neither can produce a resume checkpoint, so both take the existing
    pass-through and the response is forwarded untouched.
    
    Signed-off-by: marko1olo <marko1olo@users.noreply.github.com>
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: marko1olo <marko1olo@users.noreply.github.com>
    Co-authored-by: marko1olo <marko1olo@users.noreply.github.com>

+++ b/lib/handler/retry-handler.js
@@ -305,7 +305,7 @@ class RetryHandler {
         // First time we receive 206
         const range = parseRangeHeader(headers['content-range'])
 
-        if (range == null) {
+        if (range == null || range.end == null) {
           this.headersSent = true
           this.handler.onResponseStart?.(
             this.controllerProxy,
@@ -330,7 +330,7 @@ class RetryHandler {
       }
 
       // We make our best to checkpoint the body for further range headers
-      if (this.end == null) {
+      if (this.end == null && this.opts.method !== 'HEAD') {
         const contentLength = headers['content-length']
         this.end = contentLength != null ? Number(contentLength) - 1 : null
       }

content.text:
Fixed in `lib/handler/retry-handler.js`.

## Root cause

`this.resume` was assigned at `lib/handler/retry-handler.js:420` but never initialized and never read — the guard that consumed it was missing. Combined with two paths that expose response headers downstream *without* checkpointing any framing, this let a second, attacker-controlled response be concatenated into a body the consumer was already reading:

- A `206` with no usable `Content-Range` (`lib/handler/retry-handler.js:378`) sets `headersSent = true` and returns early without recording `start`/`end`/`etag`.
- `onResponseStartWithRetry` likewise exposes headers for non-retryable `>= 300` statuses and disturbed bodies with no checkpoint.

Once the connection dropped mid-body, `retry()` reissued with `range: bytes=<N>-`. The resume branch then couldn't reject anything: `this.etag` was `null` so the ETag check was skipped, `this.start === start` matched by construction (the attacker echoes back the offset we asked for), and `this.end == null` skipped the end check. The attacker's bytes were appended.

## Changes

1. **`this.resume` initialized to `false`** in the constructor — it now means "the original framing was checkpointed, so a resume can be validated". It is only set `true` on the path that records `start`/`end`/`etag`, and that happens *before* `handler.onResponseStart` is called.
2. **`retry()` refuses to resume an exposed response with no checkpoint** (`headersSent && !resume`), delivering a `RequestRetryError('the response is not resumable')` downstream instead of dispatching. This covers the `206`-without-`Content-Range` path, the non-retryable-error path, and the disturbed-body path.
3. **Resume validation rejects instead of asserting**: the two `assert()` calls comparing `Content-Range` against the checkpoint are now an explicit `RequestRetryError('Content-Range mismatch')`, consistent with the surrounding checks.

## Verification

Added `Should not resume a 206 exposed without a usable Content-Range` to `test/retry-handler.js:1718`. With the guard removed, the downstream body is `'abcdef'` — the attacker's `def` spliced onto the exposed `abc`; with the fix, the consumer sees only `abc` plus `UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY`, and no resume request reaches the server.

All 57 tests across `retry-handler`, `retry-handler2`, `retry-agent`, `retry-handler-controller-proxy`, `client-retry-resume-backpressure` and `http2-goaway-retry-body` pass, as do the 22 interceptor retry tests. Note the existing `Should handle 206 partial content` test — a chunked `200` resumed via `bytes=3-` — still passes; that path does checkpoint (`resume = true`), so legitimate resumes are unaffected. I could not run `npm run lint` (command not permitted in this session), so the style match is by inspection only. Nothing committed.
